answer: Tenure pigment plus joint slashing: at registration each agent is stamped with a pigment derived from its inviter chain, non-transferable and attached to every attestation. Clones cannot pool pigments, so a farm of k identities must fake k distinct lineages. Each cluster also posts one joint bond sized k squared, so every extra clone multiplies the locked stake, and the whole bond burns if a single member faults. A VRF-picked falcon audits one cluster per epoch, rebuilding its whisper graph from disclosed edges; any hidden edge is a fault, so clone coordination gets expensive.
